docs.title: YANG Version Support for IOS-XE Writers
Overview
docs.text:
IOS-XE YANG models change across firmware versions. The NAC (Network as Code) writers are authored against a baseline version (currently 17.18.2 on C9300-24P). Earlier versions (17.15, 17.16) diverge in several ways:

  • Module prefixes required on augmented JSON body keys
  • Different YANG list-key names (e.g. ordering-seq vs seq)
  • Empty-leaf encoding ([null] instead of boolean true)
  • Different container shapes (flat ↔ nested, keyed list ↔ container)
  • Different RESTCONF paths and envelope keys

docs.title: Per-family schema validation
docs.text:
CVK uses goyang-extracted, per-family Go schema packages as CI-time validators. For each config family the generator navigates the resolved native YANG entry tree to the terminal container or list declared in yang_paths, serialises that sub-tree to a gzip-JSON blob, and embeds it as a ySchema byte literal in schema.go. This approach avoids ygot code generation entirely — no 125 MB generated files, no 32 GB memory peaks.

Runtime is unchanged. The override table, map-shaped writers, and engine are not modified by this system. The generated packages are never imported at runtime — they register a cfgvalidation.FamilySchemaValidator from their init() function, and the fixture harness calls Lookup(family, releaseTag) to validate every op body against the schema during go test.

BUILD / CI TIME
  families.yaml (yang_paths per family)
      │
      ▼
  computeModuleClosure() — goyang BFS over import+include graph
      │  produces minimal module set per family
      ▼
  extractFamilySchemaEntries() — ms.Process() resolves augments;
      │  navigates nativeEntry.Dir to terminal container/list
      ▼
  buildFamilyYSchema() — gzip-JSON blob of the terminal entry sub-tree
      │
      ▼
  internal/drivers/iosxe/configdriver/generated/<release>/<family>/
    schema.go    (goyang-based gzip blob, UnzipSchema function)
    register.go  (calls cfgvalidation.Register from init())

CI VALIDATOR (fixture_test.go)
  writer.Diff() → expected_ops.json op bodies
      │
      ▼
  validateOpsAgainstGeneratedSchema()
      │
      ├── validator registered  → validateJSONEntry() — structural check
      └── no validator          → silently skipped (incremental rollout)

Generated packages live under internal/drivers/iosxe/configdriver/generated/. They are committed to the repo so runtime builds do not need the YANG source bundle. CI runs the pinned generator and verifies that the committed packages have no tracked or untracked drift. The make ygot-validate-gen RELEASE=<tag> target regenerates one release from a clean output directory.

Schema coverage limitations. Each family's schema is extracted from a module closure computed by tracing import/include graphs outward from the modules named in yang_paths. Modules that augment the native tree (e.g. Cisco-IOS-XE-aaa) are not found by this traversal unless they appear as a Module: prefix in the family's yang_paths. When augmenting modules are absent the terminal entry's Dir is empty and the validator skips that container rather than producing false positives.

Skip policy. A family is skipped (emits a compilable stub schema.go) when:

  • its yang_paths resolve to no module prefixes in the YANG directory,
  • the extracted schema blob exceeds 512 KB (e.g. system with /native as its target — the entire native tree), or
  • the path is not present in the YANG model for that release.

Those are domain limitations, not general error handling. Parser, schema-builder, filesystem, registration, and validator-index errors fail generation immediately. The exact expected release/family/reason-code set is stored in schema/yang-skip-baseline.yaml; an added skip, resolved skip, or reason change fails generation until the baseline and regenerated artifacts are intentionally updated together. generated/SKIPLIST.md is the human summary. There are currently 35 usable validators and 19 reviewed skip stubs per supported release.

Validation strictness mode. By default the validator is lenient: unknown fields and structural type mismatches are silently skipped so fixtures that reference deprecated YANG paths or fields from augmenting modules outside the closure do not fail CI. Set CVK_SCHEMA_VALIDATION=strict to enable strict mode, which reports these discrepancies as hard errors:

# Surface all YANG schema discrepancies in fixture data:
CVK_SCHEMA_VALIDATION=strict \
  go test ./internal/drivers/iosxe/configdriver/writers/... -run TestFixtures

Strict-mode failures indicate one of: - a fixture uses a field name not present in the YANG schema for that release (e.g. a deprecated or augmented field — fix by updating the fixture), - the schema closure is incomplete and the augmenting module needs to be added to the family's yang_paths (e.g. a Module:field prefix is missing).

The default lenient mode keeps CI green while these root causes are addressed incrementally. See generated/SKIPLIST.md for the current skip list.

docs.title: Intent, Translation, Validation Boundary
docs.text:
CVK keeps the public IOSXEConfig.spec.source payload in the canonical NetAsCode shape. That shape is intentionally release-stable: operators should not have to change day-0 YAML just because IOS-XE moved a leaf or renamed an augmented container between 17.18 and 26.01.

The release-specific boundary is therefore:

NetAsCode intent
  -> family writer
  -> version override / body transform
  -> IOS-XE YANG JSON op
  -> validation boundary
  -> RESTCONF / NETCONF / gNMI transport

internal/drivers/iosxe/configdriver/validation owns the validation boundary. It runs after writers emit transport.Op values and before the engine calls Apply. The default StructuralValidator checks common op invariants (path scope, JSON envelope shape, body presence) and hosts narrow release profiles for known divergences. IOS-XE 26.01 currently validates that ip_domain.name has been translated to name-container.name-no-vrf before mutation.

This is the seam where generated ygot/ytypes validators belong once per-release config model packages are available. ygot should validate the device-facing YANG payload, not replace the public NetAsCode intent model.

Validation is deployment-policy controlled:

Mode Effect CONFIG_YANG_VALIDATION=disabled default; no validation gate CONFIG_YANG_VALIDATION=warn log validation failures and continue CONFIG_YANG_VALIDATION=strict fail the family before mutation

The Helm value is config.yangValidationMode. The controller propagates it to per-device VK pods so aggregator mode and per-pod mode use the same policy.

docs.title: Stable NetAsCode Import Contract
docs.text:
For customer migrations from Terraform-based NetAsCode, CVK imports the resolved NetAsCode IOS-XE model and records provenance in IOSXEConfig.spec.modelSource. This keeps the public intent model stable while the writer layer handles IOS-XE release differences.

spec:
  modelSource:
    format: netascode-iosxe
    resolved: true
    exporter: terraform-iosxe-nac-iosxe write_model_file

resolved: false is rejected by the resolver. If a future NetAsCode release adds fields, CVK should first accept the canonical data model shape, then either translate the field for the target YANG release or report it as an unsupported family/field through migration tooling and validation. The CRD should not fork by IOS-XE release.

docs.title: Override Table (yang_version_override_table.go)
docs.text:
The declarative override table is the central registry of version- conditional YANG behaviour. Each entry targets a (family, version_range) and describes mutations to apply to the YANG wire representation.

┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Override Table Entry                │
│                                      │
│  Family:              "route_map"    │
│  MinVersion:          [17, 0]        │
│  MaxVersion:          [17, 18]       │
│  ElementMap:          { old → new }  │
│  NestedYANGInnerOverride: "..."      │
│  YANGPathOverride:    "..."          │
│  EnvelopeKeyOverride: "..."          │
│  EmptyLeaves:         ["prefer"]     │
│  BodyTransform:       func(...)      │
└──────────────────────────────────────┘

The table is resolved once at startup via ResolveForVersion(major, minor). Writers query the resolved state at Diff/Apply time:

Query Function Purpose IsLegacyVersion(fam) Is the device on a pre-baseline version? ResolvedYANGPath(fam, default) Version-correct RESTCONF path ResolvedEnvelopeKey(fam, default) Version-correct JSON envelope ResolvedNestedYANGInner(fam, default) Version-correct inner list name ApplyOverrideToBody(body, override) Full transform chain

docs.title: Custom Version-Branched Writers
docs.text:
Three families have structural YANG differences too deep for the override table alone:

Family Mechanism bgp Keyed list (17.16) vs container (17.18+) prefix_list Flat compound-keyed (17.16) vs nested (17.18+) ip_community_list Deprecated groupings (17.16) vs community-list-entry (17.18+)

These writers use IsLegacyVersion() to select their code path, and the override table provides path/envelope selection. Transform logic is per-writer.

docs.title: YAML 1.1 Boolean Key Fix
docs.text: sigs.k8s.io/yaml (YAML 1.1) interprets bare no as boolean false, which becomes map key "false" in map[string]any. This is fixed globally by intent.FixYAML11BoolKeys(), which runs once on the fully-merged configuration tree at the end of Resolver.Resolve().

docs.title: Adding Support for a New IOS-XE Version
1. Identify divergences
docs.text:
Compare the YANG schemas between the new version and the baseline:

# Download YANG models from the device
curl -k https://<device>/restconf/.well-known/host-meta

# Or use Cisco's published YANG repo:
# https://github.com/YangModels/yang/tree/main/vendor/cisco/xe

Use pyang --tree-diff or yanglint to diff specific modules:

pyang -f tree --tree-path /native/ip/prefix-list \
  Cisco-IOS-XE-native-17.16.yang \
  Cisco-IOS-XE-native-17.18.yang

For RESTCONF, probe the device directly:

# GET the schema for a specific path
curl -k -u admin:pass \
  'https://<device>/restconf/data/Cisco-IOS-XE-native:native/ip/prefix-list' \
  -H 'Accept: application/yang-data+json'

docs.title: 2. Classify the divergence
docs.text: Type Fix Mechanism Module prefix needed on element key ElementMap in override table Different YANG path or envelope YANGPathOverride / EnvelopeKeyOverride Boolean → empty leaf encoding EmptyLeaves in override table Simple container shape change BodyTransform function Key field rename KeyFieldOverride or ElementMap Deep structural difference Custom writer with IsLegacyVersion()

docs.title: 3. Add the table entry
docs.text:
Add an entry to yang_version_override_table.go:

{
    Family:     "new_family",
    MinVersion: [2]int{17, 0},
    MaxVersion: [2]int{17, 20},  // exclusive upper bound
    ElementMap: map[string]string{
        "baseline-name": "Cisco-IOS-XE-module:version-name",
    },
},

docs.title: 4. Write tests
docs.text:
• Add transform tests to version_transforms_test.go
  • Add override resolution tests to yang_version_overrides_test.go
  • Add structural validation coverage for any release-specific YANG payload shape in internal/drivers/iosxe/configdriver/validation
  • Run integration tests on a device of that version

docs.title: 5. Verify
docs.text:
# Unit tests
go test ./internal/drivers/iosxe/configdriver/writers/ -v
go test ./internal/drivers/iosxe/configdriver/validation -v

# Full build
go build ./...

# Integration tests (on lab device)
pytest tests/test_monolithic_router.py -v

docs.title: Reference: CiscoDevNet/terraform-provider-iosxe
docs.text: The Terraform provider for IOS-XE is an excellent reference for correct YANG paths and data structures. It was instrumental in discovering the 17.16 prefix-lists (plural) path with the flat compound-keyed prefixes[name, no] list.

docs.title: Reference: Known YAML 1.1 Boolean Keys
docs.text:
YAML 1.1 treats these bare tokens as booleans when used as map keys:

Token JSON key Canonical name no "false" "no" yes "true" (not used in IOS-XE schema) on "true" (not used in IOS-XE schema) off "false" (not used in IOS-XE schema)

The yaml11BoolKeyMap in intent/yaml11_fix.go maps only keys that actually appear in the IOS-XE netascode schema. Add entries there if future schema keys collide with YAML 1.1 booleans.

docs.title: NX-OS Family Reference (Beta)
docs.text:
Beta

NX-OS NXOSConfig support is a Beta runtime slice. The schema is v1alpha1, family coverage is still expanding, and wire-format behaviour may change between releases. See Production Readiness for the current scope and hardening roadmap.

Declarative NX-OS device configuration is driven by the NXOSConfig CRD over NX-API REST/DME, using the shared Network as Code config engine. Unlike the IOS-XE Family Reference — which is generated from vendored YANG across many families — the NX-OS slice currently ships a focused set of hand-written family writers.

docs.title: Supported families
docs.text:
Family Key Covers System system Device-level settings such as hostname Feature feature Individual NX-OS feature enablement (e.g. interface-vlan, lacp) Feature set feature_set Installable feature sets (e.g. fex) VLAN vlan VLAN definitions (id, name) Interface (Ethernet) interface_ethernet Ethernet interface config: description, MTU, admin state

The strict NetAsCode path emits the pinned provider's derived Layer-2/admin attributes, but refuses to convert an observed non-Layer-2 interface and requires an explicit shutdown: false before bringing up an observed shutdown port. Native CVK source preserves omitted admin/layer properties.

Each family is opt-in per NXOSConfig via spec.managedFamilies; the engine only reconciles families you list and applies the shared drift-detection contract. NX-OS revision history and rollback are not implemented yet.

For sources that declare modelSource.format: netascode-nxos, feature and feature_set leaves must use the canonical Boolean types. Provider-state strings such as enabled, disabled, installed, or uninstalled remain a native-CVK compatibility extension only and are rejected at the strict import boundary.

docs.title: Device release gate
docs.text:
NX-OS writes fail closed unless the live show version result matches an admitted profile. Admission here means the release can exercise the parity pipeline; it is not production certification of every DME mapping.

Live release pattern Maturity Model contract Evidence 10.3(9) plus an optional alphanumeric, ., _, or - suffix Admitted Beta 0.3.0 CVK Nexus 9000v lab evidence; current automated credentialed run pending 10.5(4) plus an optional alphanumeric, ., _, or - suffix Experimental, explicit opt-in 0.3.0 Upstream NetAsCode tested-version matrix and pinned static DME oracle; CVK live qualification pending

Experimental profiles are rejected by default. A lab operator can opt in to 10.5(4) with Helm value nxos.allowExperimentalReleases=true, which sets CVK_NXOS_ALLOW_EXPERIMENTAL_RELEASES=true on the controller and propagates it to per-device pods. This gate is not a production certification; leave it off until the live write/removal/rollback checklist passes for that release.

An empty version records Ready=False, reason=DeviceVersionPending and is retried automatically. A syntactically invalid result records MalformedDeviceVersion; a well-formed release outside the table records UnsupportedDeviceVersion. Both rejected states remain Pending and cannot reach a writer mutation. If spec.targetYangVersion is set, it must equal the normalized live release profile; it cannot be used to select a different DME shape than the running device.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
apiVersion: config.cisco.vk/v1alpha1
kind: NXOSConfig
metadata:
  name: nexus9300v-vlans
  namespace: default
spec:
  deviceRef:
    name: nexus9300v-01
  managedFamilies:
    - system
    - vlan
    - interface_ethernet
  driftPolicy: revert
  driftDetectInterval: 5m
  writeStartup: true
  modelSource:
    format: netascode-nxos
    modelVersion: 0.3.0
    schemaDigest: sha256:5d5482679fb28e751d34cdc49342f8434914a7714966ba8244923b95d678698d
    resolved: true
    exporter: example-customer-exporter@0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
    sourceRevision: 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
  source:
    inline:
      system:
        hostname: nexus9300v-01
      vlan:
        vlans:
          - id: 3903
            name: CVK_LAB
      interfaces:
        ethernets:
          - id: 1/1
            description: CVK lab uplink
            shutdown: false
            mtu: 9216

docs.title: v2026.9.0 — unpublished candidate
docs.text:
The signed v2026.9.0 tag triggered the release workflow on 2026-09-01, but the workflow stopped in its draft-visibility preflight. No controller image, Helm chart, kubectl plugin archive, SBOM, signature, provenance, or other release asset was built, pushed, signed, staged, or published by that run.

The immutable tag remains as release-history evidence and will not be moved or deleted. Its GitHub draft has zero attached assets and will not be published. No Krew update was triggered for this candidate; at the time, the official index remained at v2026.8.1. Do not use v2026.9.0 installation URLs or version selectors.

The preflight permission correction was first carried by the also-unpublished v2026.9.1 security candidate. The complete, remediated September product update is carried by v2026.9.2, whose product delta is measured from the last official release, v2026.8.1.

docs.title: v2026.9.1 — unpublished security candidate
docs.text:
Candidate build date: 2026-09-01

The signed v2026.9.1 tag completed the release workflow, staged the expected 16-asset draft, and pushed signed controller-image and OCI-chart tags. During the required pre-publication review, the release-image scan reported two versioned dependency findings for which fixes were available:

  • CRITICAL CVE-2026-56854 in golang.org/x/crypto v0.52.0, fixed in v0.55.0.
  • HIGH CVE-2026-46600 in golang.org/x/net v0.55.0, fixed in v0.56.0.

Symbol-aware govulncheck found no reachable vulnerable call path in the controller: the reported SSH path is server-only while CVK uses SSH client APIs, and the reported DNS message symbols are not called. Even so, maintainers made a no-go decision because a release with fixed HIGH/CRITICAL dependency findings should not be published.

The immutable tag and draft are retained as release-history evidence and will not be moved, deleted, or published. No release: published event occurred, so no documentation deployment or Krew update was triggered for v2026.9.1. Do not use its image, chart, draft assets, download URLs, or installation selectors.

The older workflow emitted the mutable 2026.9 and latest image aliases before its advisory scan, so those aliases can temporarily resolve to this unpublished candidate during recovery. Do not advertise or use them, and do not rerun the v2026.9.1 tag workflow: a rerun could move the aliases again outside the corrected release gates. The v2026.9.2 workflow replaces them only after both image platforms and the complete staged candidate pass.

The remediated September release is v2026.9.2. Its product delta remains measured from the last official release, v2026.8.1.

docs.title: v2026.9.2 release notes
docs.text:
Release date: 2026-09-01

Availability: Use this release only when v2026.9.2 appears on the public Releases page. If it is not listed there, the candidate has not been published and its tag, image, chart, and download URLs must not be used.

Recovery from the unpublished September candidates: The signed v2026.9.0 workflow stopped in draft-visibility preflight before it built or staged any artifact. The corrected v2026.9.1 workflow completed, staged the expected 16 draft assets, and pushed signed image and OCI chart tags, but its pre-publication image scan found fixed HIGH/CRITICAL dependency findings. Maintainers therefore made a no-go decision. Neither draft was published, and neither candidate triggered documentation deployment or a Krew update. Their immutable tags will not be moved or deleted. v2026.9.2 contains the dependency remediation and is the replacement September release; its product delta is measured from the last official release, v2026.8.1.

This update adds an Alpha controller-extension foundation and inspectable controller build identity, and strengthens source installation, release provenance, vulnerability gating, and redistributed licensing. It retains the existing IOS-XE, NX-OS, credential-rotation, telemetry, operations, and software lifecycle functionality from v2026.8.1.

docs.title: In plain English: what is new since v2026.8.1
docs.text:
• You get two new Kubernetes CRD contracts and the manager scaffold needed for future external-controller integrations. You do not get a working Catalyst Center, APIC, Meraki, or other controller adapter in this release.
  • IOS-XE and NX-OS device behavior is unchanged. Automatic rollout after a referenced credential Secret changes already existed in v2026.8.1; this release documents that behavior and its security boundary more clearly.
  • The dependencies implicated by the rejected v2026.9.1 image findings are upgraded, and both controller-image architectures now have hard HIGH/CRITICAL vulnerability gates before merge and during release.
  • Controller and plugin version reporting, reproducible packaging, signing, provenance checks, and redistributed license material are more strictly verified. These changes make the same deliverables easier to inspect and trust; they do not add new device commands.
  • The release publishes rebuilt v2026.9.2 plugin archives. After publication, automation opens the normal upstream Krew index update PR; Krew users receive v2026.9.2 only after that PR merges. The plugin's commands and supported platforms are unchanged.
  • Existing Helm installations must apply the two new CRDs before upgrading. Fresh installations receive them from the chart automatically.

docs.title: Alpha network-controller extension foundation
docs.text:
Two new namespaced CRDs establish a generic boundary for future external controller integrations:

  • NetworkController (cisco.vk/v1alpha1) declares an HTTPS endpoint, adapter type, credential and trust references, connection limits, and administrator-approved intent Secret aliases.
  • NetworkControllerConfig (config.cisco.vk/v1alpha1) carries resolved, explicitly versioned controller-centric Network as Code intent, managed sections, ownership, and policy.

The manager includes adapter registration contracts, duplicate-endpoint fencing, isolated per-endpoint worker orchestration, material-rotation handling, and fail-closed validation. These are extension contracts, not a product integration: the v2026.9.2 image contains zero product adapters and cannot contact or mutate an external controller. The shipped boundary is report-only; apply, prune, remote-delete behavior, and mutation RBAC remain unimplemented.

See the Network Controller Extension Guide and CRD Reference.

docs.title: Existing device-credential rollout clarified
docs.text:
This rollout behavior is not new in v2026.9.2: v2026.8.1 already watched referenced credential Secrets. Updating a Secret referenced by CiscoDevice.spec.credentialSecretRef causes the manager to update the pod-template cisco.vk/credential-resource-version annotation and roll every affected VK Deployment. An explicit kubectl rollout restart is no longer part of the normal credential-rotation path.

This release clarifies the security boundary around that existing behavior. The manager observes a typed Secret object's resourceVersion; reconciliation does not inspect .data, but Secret data can still enter the manager's cache/API client. The manager's Secret RBAC and memory therefore remain in the credential trust boundary. See Bulk rotation and Security principles.

docs.title: Dependency remediation and hard vulnerability gates
docs.text:
• The controller moves from golang.org/x/crypto v0.52.0 to v0.55.0 and selects golang.org/x/net v0.57.0. The separate Terraform helper moves from golang.org/x/net v0.55.0 to the fixed v0.56.0.
  • These updates remediate the versioned dependencies reported for CVE-2026-56854 and CVE-2026-46600 in the unpublished v2026.9.1 image. Symbol-aware govulncheck found no reachable vulnerable call path in that candidate, but maintainers declined to publish while fixed HIGH/CRITICAL dependencies remained.
  • The required pre-merge controller-image scans and the exact tagged-image scans now fail on any fixed HIGH/CRITICAL finding on either Linux AMD64 or ARM64. This supplements the existing symbol-aware controller and Terraform govulncheck gates. Mutable 2026.9 and latest image aliases move only after both platform scans and all chart, plugin, and curated-draft staging complete successfully.

docs.title: Verifiable build identity and distribution hardening
docs.text:
• Release-built cisco-vk version and cisco-vk --version report the exact release tag, full source commit, and reproducible RFC3339 UTC build time. Direct development builds identify themselves as devel.
  • The existing Linux AMD64/ARM64 non-root controller images now use a pinned Go 1.26.7 builder and digest-pinned builder/runtime bases, use reproducible build flags, and redistribute the project, dependency, Go toolchain, NOTICE, and patent material applicable to their binaries.
  • The existing plugin archives remain available for Linux and macOS on AMD64 and ARM64. They now include applicable Go license/patent files and undergo exact archive installation and execution checks through Krew; Windows remains unsupported.
  • Signed image, chart, checksum, plugin, SBOM, and provenance artifacts already existed in v2026.8.1. This release strengthens their immutable tool pins, draft/asset checks, and pre- and post-publication verification.
  • The source installer now checksum-verifies Linux AMD64/ARM64 Go downloads, installs a private versioned toolchain without replacing /usr/local/go, and limits itself to building and installing the binary. It no longer tries to create TLS files or a systemd unit; Helm remains the supported cluster installation path.
  • Documentation build dependencies and browser assets are pinned and license-checked. The website dependency updates include the nanoid 3.3.18 security fix. Generated IOS-XE family-page additions document fields that the runtime already supported; they do not add device behavior.

See the CLI and plugin reference, Getting Started, and the project licensing summary.

docs.title: Required upgrade action: apply both new CRDs first
docs.text:
Helm installs files under crds/ on a fresh installation but does not apply new or updated CRDs during helm upgrade. An existing installation must apply the NetworkController and NetworkControllerConfig CRDs before upgrading.

After the release is published:

kubectl apply --server-side -f \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cisco-open/cisco-virtual-kubelet/v2026.9.2/config/crd/cisco.vk_networkcontrollers.yaml
kubectl apply --server-side -f \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cisco-open/cisco-virtual-kubelet/v2026.9.2/config/crd/config.cisco.vk_networkcontrollerconfigs.yaml

kubectl wait --for=condition=Established --timeout=60s \
  crd/networkcontrollers.cisco.vk \
  crd/networkcontrollerconfigs.config.cisco.vk

helm upgrade cvk \
  oci://ghcr.io/cisco-open/charts/cisco-virtual-kubelet \
  --version 2026.9.2 \
  --namespace cvk-system \
  --reuse-values --wait --timeout 5m

kubectl rollout restart \
  deployment/cvk-cisco-virtual-kubelet-controller \
  --namespace cvk-system
kubectl rollout status \
  deployment/cvk-cisco-virtual-kubelet-controller \
  --namespace cvk-system --timeout=5m

If either new CRD is absent when the new manager first starts, existing CiscoDevice reconcilers continue running, but NetworkController registration is disabled for that process. Apply the CRDs and restart the manager to enable the Alpha scaffold. The restart does not add a product adapter or enable external-controller mutations.

For a release name other than cvk, resolve the controller Deployment from its Helm labels instead of copying the example name. See Upgrading CRDs for the complete procedure and rollback cautions.

docs.title: Compatibility and security notes
docs.text:
• Source builds require Go 1.26.7 or a later 1.26 patch, or Go 1.27.0 or a later 1.27 patch. The release build is pinned to Go 1.26.7.
  • Chart users need Helm 3.21+ or 4.2+. The release is validated with exact Helm 3.21.4 and 4.2.4 binaries.
  • The two new CRDs use CEL transition rules for immutable identity fields. Kubernetes 1.29 or later supports this behavior as GA. On Kubernetes 1.28, CustomResourceValidationExpressions must remain enabled.
  • Controller workers use namespace-scoped RBAC and caches. Endpoints or config authors that do not trust one another should use separate namespaces.
  • Duplicate fencing compares the exact stored endpoint string only within one namespace; it does not normalize equivalent URLs or coordinate across namespaces or clusters.
  • Network-controller credentials and intent values are projected into a worker by the kubelet. The Alpha runtime must not emit desired or observed values in status, events, or logs.
  • No IOS-XE YANG source or generated schema source changed from v2026.8.1. The existing generated material retains its recorded upstream provenance and applicable licensing notices.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• No Catalyst Center, APIC, Meraki, or other product adapter ships in this release. NetworkController and NetworkControllerConfig alone are not a usable controller integration.
  • Network-controller apply, prune, and remote-delete operations are reserved for future gated implementations. The current foundation is report-only.
  • Helm upgrades require the explicit CRD application and manager restart described above. Helm rollback does not remove CRDs or stored custom resources.
  • The kubectl plugin's ad-hoc exec command is IOS-XE-only, read-only, and requires the per-device deployment mode. Windows plugin archives are not produced.
  • NX-OS, device configuration, operational actions, software lifecycle, and telemetry surfaces retain the maturity levels documented in Feature Maturity; their v1alpha1 APIs may continue to evolve.
